prompt: Flashcards for Dutch kitchen words with the English on the back: lepel/spoon, vork/fork, mes/knife, bord/plate, kopje/cup, pan/pan.
A deck called "Swahili Basics" with jambo/hello, asante/thank you, rafiki/friend, chakula/food, maji/water, and nyumba/house.

Earth science flashcards: subduction, rift valley, transform fault, mantle convection, each with its definition on the back. Subduction is one plate sliding beneath another into the mantle; a rift valley is a lowland formed where plates pull apart; a transform fault is where plates slide past each other sideways; mantle convection is the slow circulation of hot rock that drives plate motion.

Networking terms for my IT certification: router, switch, firewall, DNS, DHCP. Back of each card: forwards packets between networks; connects devices within one network; filters traffic by rules; translates domain names to IP addresses; hands out IP addresses automatically. Add the instruction "Define each term in your own words before flipping."

Flashcards for basic antiderivatives, rendered as math: the integral of x^n dx is x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C, the integral of 1/x dx is ln|x| + C, the integral of e^x dx is e^x + C, the integral of cos x dx is sin x + C.
Dark deck titled "Exponent Laws": a^m · a^n = a^(m+n), a^m / a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), a^0 = 1, a^(−n) = 1/a^n. Put the left side on the front and the simplified form on the back, as math.

Physics constants deck: speed of light / $c \approx 3.00 \times 10^8$ m/s; gravitational acceleration at Earth's surface / $g \approx 9.81$ m/s²; Planck's constant / $h \approx 6.63 \times 10^{-34}$ J·s; Avogadro's number / $N_A \approx 6.02 \times 10^{23}$ per mole.

Flashcards pairing inventions with their inventors: telephone/Alexander Graham Bell, phonograph/Thomas Edison, World Wide Web/Tim Berners-Lee, printing press/Johannes Gutenberg, polio vaccine/Jonas Salk.

Space race dates — the event on the front, the year on the back: Sputnik 1 launched (1957), Yuri Gagarin orbits Earth (1961), first spacewalk (1965), Apollo 11 Moon landing (1969), Apollo–Soyuz docking (1975).
Flag flashcards titled "Flags of the World": the flag on the front and the country on the back, for Kenya, India, Mexico, Norway and South Korea.

Bird identification deck, photo on the front and the species on the back: https://cdn.harbourbirdclub.org/cards/robin-320.jpg is a European robin, https://cdn.harbourbirdclub.org/cards/wren-320.jpg is a wren, and https://cdn.harbourbirdclub.org/cards/blue-tit-320.jpg is a blue tit.
Make a deck of knot pictures with the knot's name on the back — bowline, clove hitch, reef knot, figure-eight. I don't have the photos yet.

Molecule flashcards with the name on the front and the structure image on the back: water is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Water_molecule_3D.svg/330px-Water_molecule_3D.svg.png and methane is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Methane-CRC-MW-3D-balls.png/330px-Methane-CRC-MW-3D-balls.png.

Light-themed deck titled "Cooking Terms" with the instruction "Picture the technique, then flip.": braise / brown then cook slowly in a little liquid; blanch / boil briefly then plunge into ice water; deglaze / loosen browned bits from a pan with liquid; julienne / cut into thin matchsticks.

Study cards for my driving theory test, a question on the front and the full answer on the back: What should you do at a flashing amber light? — Give way to pedestrians still crossing, then proceed if the way is clear. When must you use dipped headlights during the day? — When visibility is seriously reduced, generally under 100 metres. What is the stopping distance at 30 mph? — About 23 metres, six car lengths.
Square roots drill: the front shows √1 through √144 for the perfect squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144, and the back shows the root.

I've written these as definition then word — please make flashcards: "a word that sounds like another but has a different meaning" — homophone; "a word with the opposite meaning" — antonym; "a word formed from the first letters of other words" — acronym; "a word that imitates a sound" — onomatopoeia.
Just one flashcard: front "Pythagorean theorem", back "$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$".
Add two more cards — Ottawa for Canada and Canberra for Australia — and title the deck "Capitals".
Switch this deck to dark mode, and the back of the "tachycardia" card is wrong — it should say "a resting heart rate above 100 beats per minute".
